references.text: Jacob blesses Joseph and mentions blessings from the womb and from the breasts, which relates to fertility and offspring.
God promises that no woman shall be barren or lose her child, and that He will fill the number of their days—a parallel to the blessing over the fruit of the womb.
God promises to make the people fruitful and numerous as part of the covenant, which corresponds with the blessing over offspring.
An almost identical blessing over the fruit of the womb, the produce of the ground, the herds, the oxen, and the flocks as a reward for obedience.
Elaborates on the same blessing by mentioning abundance in the fruit of the womb, the herds, and the produce of the ground.
Repeats the promise of blessing over the fruit of the womb, the herds, and the produce of the ground when the people turn back to the Lord.
Children are described as an inheritance from the Lord, the fruit of the womb as a reward, which reflects the blessing over offspring.
The one who fears the Lord is blessed with a fruitful wife and children—a parallel to the blessing over the fruit of the womb.
Elizabeth praises Mary as blessed among women and calls the fruit of her womb blessed, with a clear linguistic parallel to the Hebrew text.
